To draw the isometric view of the combination of solids:

1. **Convert to Isometric Scale:** Use true dimensions or standard isometric conversion ($1 = \frac{\sqrt{2}}{\sqrt{3}}$ or simply use the isometric scale). 

2. **Draw the Base (Hexagonal Prism):** 
   - Draw an isometric box (enclosing rectangle) for a hexagon of side $35\text{ mm}$. 
   - Construct the isometric view of the hexagonal base such that one of the sides is perpendicular to the V.P. direction.
   - Extrude the prism vertically upwards by its height of $40\text{ mm}$ by projecting all six corners up and completing the top hexagonal face.

3. **Place the Cone Centrally on Top:** 
   - Locate the exact geometric center of the top hexagonal face by drawing diagonals.
   - From this center, measure vertically upwards along the isometric axis by the cone's height ($60\text{ mm}$) to locate the apex of the cone.
   - Draw the isometric view of the circular base of diameter $50\text{ mm}$ (which appears as an ellipse in isometric) centered appropriately, and draw tangents from the apex to the elliptical base to complete the right circular cone.
proTip: Always construct the four-center method for drawing isometric circles (ellipses) accurately.
